prompt: The attached images are the official character portraits: keep each character's design, colors, markings and accessories exactly as in their portrait (the portraits only show the head; draw the rest of the body to match). Ignore any badge, medallion or hexagon frame around a portrait: it is not part of the character. A single comic-book panel from the cozy story mode of the game Dice Duel. It must look like the game's own art, the attached character art: a flat sticker illustration with a thick uniform dark cocoa outline (#3a2a2e) around every shape, flat color fills with ONE soft cel-shaded shadow tone and one small highlight, no gradients, no glow, no painterly texture, no realistic lighting, no 3D rendering. Only the game's palette: cream paper #fbf1df and #f1dfc2, ivory #fffaf0, sage felt greens #4e7d68 and #5f8f78, wood browns #7a4b2f and #a86c45, honey #f2b15e, coral #e8806f, rose #ec8fa8, sky blue #6fbfd3, lavender #b8a4f0, mint #8fd6a8, cocoa #3a2a2e. Backgrounds are SIMPLE: a few big flat color shapes (a wall, a floor, a window) with at most three props, no clutter, no decorative plants or mugs unless the scene asks for them. Cozy, adult, dry humor; expressive faces, not chibi, not childish. No halftone dots (they are added later), no panel border, no frame, no gutter, no white margin: the art fills the image edge to edge. No speech balloons, no captions, no sound effects and no lettering, except a sign the scene explicitly asks for. Every die is a plain six-sided cube with round pips, in its owner's color (Diana's are pink). Draw few dice, and every visible face with a correct standard pip layout: 1 = one center pip; 2 = two pips on a diagonal; 3 = three pips on a diagonal; 4 = four corners; 5 = four corners and the center; 6 = two parallel rows of three. Never more than six pips on a face, never a blank face, and two faces of the same die never show numbers that add up to 7. RAPOSA: an anthropomorphic red fox with half-closed contented eyes and a dark-green knitted scarf; elegant and pleased with herself. SCENE: Raposa the fox lounges on a plush old sofa inside a warm winter den, eyes half closed, satisfied and elegant, one paw on the armrest. Her single big bushy tail curls ONCE around her body and rests on the sofa cushion in front of her, clearly attached at her lower back, white tip visible: one simple readable silhouette, nothing tangled. A few frog-green dice on a small side table.
